Work in C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod (Next.js 16 + Prisma, an AI website builder called Kodely).

BUILD: two Builder/Editor features. Bundled because both touch `app/projects/[id]/Editor.tsx` and parallel edits there would collide.

## 1. Diff view — see what changed before and after a build
Today a build rewrites files and the user sees only the preview. There is no way to know *what* changed. `Build.filesSnapshot` already stores the complete file tree after every successful build (see `prisma/schema.prisma`), and `app/api/projects/[id]/builds/[buildId]/restore/route.ts` already restores from it — so the data for a diff exists and nothing reads it that way.

Build a per-build diff: which files changed, added, removed, and a readable line-level diff for each. **No diff library** — hand-roll a simple LCS or line-based diff; the files are small.

The board card is "Diff view with approve / reject before applying". Read it and be honest in your report about whether approve/reject is achievable: the build has already written to the database by the time the user sees anything, so "reject" means restoring the previous snapshot, not preventing a write. If that is what you build, say that is what it is — do not present a restore as a pre-apply gate.

## 2. Undo / redo across AI and manual edits
`Build.filesSnapshot` gives you a checkpoint per successful build, and History already lists them. What is missing is a cheap one-step undo — "that last change was wrong, put it back" — without opening History and picking.

Note `app/api/projects/[id]/builds/route.ts` now filters to builds whose snapshot still exists (the retention job clears old ones), so an undo target can legitimately disappear. Handle that honestly rather than showing a control that fails.

## Scope — ONLY files under `app/projects/[id]/`
READ anything. If you need an API route outside that directory, describe it precisely in your report rather than creating it.

## Do not regress — this file is dense now
Read `Editor.tsx` in full first. It carries: live progress narration, building overlay, thumbs-up/down, zip download, Enhance/Revert, low-credit warning, Stop/cancel, device-frame preview, ⌘K command palette, connection-loss recovery, a cost estimate, an SEO panel, a Brand panel, a Submissions link with unread count, and click-to-edit selection. **All of it must keep working.**

Traps already hit in this exact file:
- Two `aria-live` regions with the same string made screen readers announce every progress line twice. There is exactly one for progress now — keep it that way.
- The command palette went keyboard-dead when focus was outside the dialog; the window-level Escape net is load-bearing.
- The preview is now delivered via `srcdoc` with everything inlined, because the iframe is opaque-origin and cannot load subresources. Do not "simplify" that back to `src` — it would blank the preview, which was broken that way for months.

## Constraints
- Preserve the accessibility bar: `focus-visible:` states, real labels, `aria-*` on stateful controls, no keyboard traps.
- **No new white text on the brand gradient** (fails contrast — known accepted issue).
- Known pre-existing: the sidebar is `w-96` so there is overflow at 380px. Do not worsen it; do not attempt the responsive rework.
- No new npm dependencies. Do NOT run `npm run build`, `git commit`, `git push`, or `deploy.sh`.
- **HARD GATE: `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx eslint app lib components`, and `node --import ./scripts/test/register.mjs --test "tests/*.test.mjs"` must ALL pass — currently 0 errors, 0 warnings, 209 tests.** If your diff algorithm is pure, add tests for it under `tests/`.

## Report back
Both features, your honest verdict on approve/reject, how you handle a pruned snapshot, what you verified in the running app, and confirmation the existing features still work.

Welcome to the Next.js documentation!

## What is Next.js?

Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. You use React Components to build user interfaces, and Next.js for additional features and optimizations.

It also automatically configures lower-level tools like bundlers and compilers. You can instead focus on building your product and shipping quickly.

Whether you're an individual developer or part of a larger team, Next.js can help you build interactive, dynamic, and fast React applications.

## How to use the docs

The docs are organized into 3 sections:

- [Getting Started](/docs/app/getting-started): Step-by-step tutorials to help you create a new application and learn the core Next.js features.
- [Guides](/docs/app/guides): Tutorials on specific use cases, choose what's relevant to you.
- [API Reference](/docs/app/api-reference): Detailed technical reference for every feature.

Use the sidebar to navigate through the sections, or search (`Ctrl+K` or `Cmd+K`) to quickly find a page.

## App Router and Pages Router

Next.js has two different routers:

- **App Router**: The newer router that supports new React features like Server Components.
- **Pages Router**: The original router, still supported and being improved.

At the top of the sidebar, you'll notice a dropdown menu that allows you to switch between the [App Router](/docs/app) and the [Pages Router](/docs/pages) docs.

### React version handling

The App Router and Pages Router handle React versions differently:

- **App Router**: Uses [React canary releases](https://react.dev/blog/2023/05/03/react-canaries) built-in, which include all the stable React 19 changes, as well as newer features being validated in frameworks, prior to a new React release.

- **Pages Router**: Uses the React version installed in your project's `package.json`.

This approach ensures new React features work reliably in the App Router while maintaining backwards compatibility for existing Pages Router applications.

## Pre-requisite knowledge

Our documentation assumes some familiarity with web development. Before getting started, it'll help if you're comfortable with:

- HTML
- CSS
- JavaScript
- React

If you're new to React or need a refresher, we recommend starting with our [React Foundations course](/learn/react-foundations), and the [Next.js Foundations course](/learn/dashboard-app) that has you building an application as you learn.

## Accessibility

For the best experience when using a screen reader, we recommend using Firefox and NVDA, or Safari and VoiceOver.

## Join our Community

If you have questions about anything related to Next.js, you're always welcome to ask our community on [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions), [Discord](https://discord.com/invite/bUG2bvbtHy), [X (Twitter)](https://x.com/nextjs), and [Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/nextjs).

## What I built

**Files** — modified `app/projects/[id]/Editor.tsx` and `app/projects/[id]/page.tsx`; added `app/projects/[id]/diff.ts`, `app/projects/[id]/diff-actions.ts`, `app/projects/[id]/DiffView.tsx`, `tests/build-diff.test.mjs`. **No API route was created** — the diff is read through a Server Action in `app/projects/[id]/diff-actions.ts`, which keeps everything inside the allowed directory. No new dependencies.

### 1. Diff view
`diff.ts` is a pure, hand-rolled LCS line diff (no library): common prefix/suffix stripped first, then a flat `Uint32Array` DP over the changed middle, grouped into 3-line-context hunks with real 1-based line numbers on both sides. Two independent bounds keep the Server Action payload sane — an LCS matrix cap (falls back to a flagged whole-block replace) and a per-file/whole-build rendered-line budget (drops hunks, keeps exact +/− counts). Unchanged files never appear.

`loadBuildDiff(projectId, buildId)` re-checks the session and scopes by `project.userId` (a Server Action is a POST anyone can send; the button is not the boundary). It diffs the **source** trees of the build's snapshot and the newest earlier surviving snapshot. Entry points: "See what changed" under a finished build, a "Changes" button per History row, and a palette command.

### 2. Undo / redo
Undo is defined over checkpoints, because a build snapshot is the only restorable state this product has. `page.tsx` seeds the timeline and answers one question exactly — *does the draft still match the newest checkpoint?* — by comparing the trees server-side (`sameTree`), not by guessing from timestamps. From there the cursor is a fact the component maintains itself. Undo/Redo sit above the prompt box (only once a checkpoint exists), each labelled with its actual target; both are also palette commands. Restore/Undo/Redo all funnel through one `applyCheckpoint`.

Manual Brand/SEO saves now go through `onManualSave` instead of `refreshFiles`, so the cursor learns the draft drifted. **Undo can put a manual edit back; nothing can redo it** — nothing captured it — so redo is cleared and says so rather than offering a step that would skip the edit.

## Honest verdict on approve / reject

**Approve/reject before applying is not achievable, and I did not build it.** By the time anything is on screen the build has written `ProjectFile` rows, charged credits, and the preview is already showing the new site. There is no pending state to gate. So the controls are **"Undo this build"** and **"Close"**, and the panel says so in as many words: *"This build has already been applied… Undoing does not cancel it and does not refund its credits; it writes the previous checkpoint back over the draft."* "Undo this build" is only offered when it is truthful — when the draft is actually at that build and a checkpoint sits directly behind it; otherwise it is withheld with the reason. A real pre-apply gate would need the generate route to stage writes instead of committing them, which is outside this directory.

## Pruned snapshots

Three distinct honest outcomes, all verified against the running app:
- **Build's own snapshot pruned** → the diff returns a specific message ("cleared to save storage"), not "not found".
- **Predecessor pruned** → `previousPruned: true`, and the panel says the whole tree is shown *because there is nothing left to compare against* — deliberately distinguished from a genuine first checkpoint, which reads differently.
- **Target pruned between list and click** → the restore route 404s; `applyCheckpoint` catches that specifically, refreshes the timeline (which drops the row), removes it from the redo stack, and reports it. With one checkpoint left, Undo disables with "this is the first checkpoint".

## Verified in the running app

The dev server on :3003 is this tree and hot-reloaded the work. Against a seeded three-build project I confirmed, end to end: the SSR undo control naming the correct target; the builds API returning three checkpoints; the **Server Action invoked over HTTP** returning correct add/remove/modify classification, hunk headers and line numbers for a modify build, an add+delete build, and the first checkpoint; then, after pruning snapshots one at a time, each of the three pruned outcomes above; and a restore round-trip (`src/legacy.ts` disappearing and returning) with the label correctly switching to "restore the last build" after a restore-then-reload.

**One honesty bug this caught and I fixed:** after restore-then-reload the server only knows "draft ≠ newest checkpoint", not where it is — the label originally said "back to the last build" when the last build was *forwards*. It now reads "restore the last build", which is true in both cases.

**Not visually confirmed:** the rendered DiffView. Setting a session cookie in the automation browser was denied by the permission classifier, and I won't enter credentials, so I verified the data path and the SSR chrome over HTTP instead.

The SSR editor still carries the palette trigger with `aria-keyshortcuts`, the view group with `aria-pressed`, the Submissions link and badge, the credit strip, Enhance/Revert, the cost estimate, "Apply change", SEO/Brand panels and click-to-edit.
